money_at_stake.rationale: The occurrence's own headline figure is well above the GT_100B threshold and traces directly to the official Xinhua News Agency account of the 2025-07-19 groundbreaking, as reported by Bloomberg: a total planned investment of 1.2 trillion yuan (USD 167 billion) for the Yarlung Tsangpo mega-dam, with China Yajiang Group unveiled the same day as the project's builder and operator. This is a single figure, not a sum of separately funded programs, and it comfortably clears GT_100B ($100B+) rather than sitting near the B10_100 boundary. Two additional citations that had corroborated details beyond this core figure were dropped this run because their own source text does not support what they were cited for: a Shanghai Metals Market article on China Yajiang Group's formation, fetched directly, confirms only the company's formation date and purpose and states no investment figure, capacity figure, or construction-period length (the 1.2 trillion yuan / 70-81 GW / ten-year figures it had been cited for are simply not in the article); and a CNBC piece on the project's cascade-station count and capacity is paywalled past its own headline in both a live fetch (HTTP 403) and the Wayback Machine's earliest capture from the day of publication, so its body claims could not be checked against its own source this run.

evidence.claim: Chinese Premier Li Qiang launched construction of the Yarlung Tsangpo mega-dam in Tibet on Saturday, with a total planned investment of 1.2 trillion yuan ($167 billion), and China Yajiang Group was unveiled the same day as the entity that will build and operate it.
evidence.source_name: Bloomberg, China Kicks Off Controversial Mega-Dam Project in Tibet
source_excerpt: Chinese Premier Li Qiang launched construction of a mega-dam project in the lower reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo river in Tibet on Saturday, with a total planned investment of 1.2 trillion yuan ($167 billion), according to the official Xinhua News Agency.

A new company called China Yajiang Group was also officially unveiled on Saturday. It will be responsible for constructing the hydro project, consisting of five cascade dams and located in the city of Nyingchi in the southeast of the autonomous region of Tibet, Xinhua said.

public_reach.rationale: Mixed and clearly reachable, not dominated by a single unlisted or sanctioned owner the way the Arctic NSR occurrence is. The project owner, China Yajiang Group, is a newly formed unlisted central SOE and holds the largest single unreachable slice: overall project financing, land, and dam-structure ownership. The market itself treated the occurrence as reaching listed issuers within days of the announcement: the wider China infrastructure-construction and hydropower sector re-rated when trading resumed the Monday after the Saturday groundbreaking, and Power Construction Corporation of China (PowerChina), the SOE named the project's main contractor (see capture_odds), jumped 10 percent to hit the daily trading limit on both that Monday and Tuesday. Not scored above 60 because the single biggest capex line, the dam's civil structure and its financing, sits with the unlisted project-owner SOE and with policy-bank lending rather than public-market revenue recognition, and because two citations that had named specific equipment-tier beneficiaries beyond PowerChina were dropped this run: a CNBC piece is paywalled past its own headline in both a live fetch and the Wayback Machine's earliest capture, and an iTiger report on a Huaxin Cement stock move returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch with no Wayback snapshot available. Neither claim could be checked against its own source text, so neither is kept on an unopened page.

capture_odds.rationale: Genuinely split between two structurally different parts of the same chain, so scored at the 'some specs, mostly price-taker' anchor rather than rounded toward the headline story. Against capture: the single largest and most directly named listed beneficiary, PowerChina, is explicitly described as the main participant expected to benefit from Yaxia hydropower construction, yet its own 2025 interim filing shows net income attributable to parent down 13.81% year over year even as revenue rose 2.66%, and its engineering-contracting segment carries the company's lowest gross margin (8.46%, versus 45.05% for power investment and operation), the standard signature of a state-directed, competitively tendered EPC business where volume does not convert into profit. For capture: the equipment layers behind the EPC headline carry real qualification barriers, UHVDC converter-valve packages at the 800kV-class scale are won by a small set of qualified suppliers (illustrated by Rongxin Huiko's award of the converter-valve package on a separate, comparable +/-800kV/8GW UHV VSC-HVDC project), and extreme-head, high-capacity hydro turbine manufacture sits with only two or three domestic makers. Scored at 45 rather than lower because those equipment niches are real, and rather than higher because the largest, most visible listed exposure to this specific occurrence is evidence of margin pressure, not margin capture.

timing_fit.rationale: Measured against this occurrence's own anchor_date (2025-07-19) and its stated window (construction 2025 to early 2030s, with procurement and transmission-corridor decisions in 2026-2028), real capital is already moving inside the horizon rather than merely projected into it. China Yajiang Group was unveiled as the project's builder on the same Saturday as groundbreaking, per Bloomberg's account of the official Xinhua announcement, and a directly connected power-evacuation asset, the 2,681km Xizang-Guangdong UHVDC transmission line, broke ground on 2025-09-16, less than two months later and squarely inside the 2-5 year window from anchor. Not scored above 75 because a megaproject of this scale (1.2 trillion yuan, five cascade dams) plausibly extends equipment procurement past the 5-year mark for its later stages, but this run found no dated, cited source confirming a specific commissioning year or construction-period length for the dam itself, nor a dated contract award for the specific turbine and tunnel-boring-machine equipment lines. A citation that had stated a roughly ten-year construction period was dropped this run: fetched directly, its source (the Shanghai Metals Market article on China Yajiang Group's formation) confirms only the company's formation date and states no construction-period length.

notes.text: No taste.md rule applies to this occurrence: TASTE-001 (rare-earth miners) and TASTE-002 (Taiwan chip-concentration) are both inapplicable on their face, so no filter was applied. REACHABLE, not PRIME, because capture_odds sits at 45: the equipment-supplier niches (turbines, UHVDC converter gear, TBMs) carry real qualification barriers, but the largest and most directly named listed beneficiary, PowerChina, is explicitly disclosing margin and net-income pressure in its own 2025 interim filing even as it is named the main contractor. A chain build here should weight the equipment-supplier links (hydro turbines, UHVDC transmission gear, cement/materials, TBMs) over the EPC/civil-construction link on capture grounds, which is roughly consistent with the heat scores already on data/chains/tibet-mega-dam.json (hydro-turbines and cement-materials read CROWDED, civil-construction and yajiang-developer read EMERGING/CROWDED, while global-hydro-spillover is the chain's one UNDISCOVERED money-corner link).
